result.rationale: The diff shows zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts now wraps the axios refresh call with refreshOAuthTokens(...). In sync mode (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId), refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, which has no `.data` property, yet the code immediately after does `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)`. So `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is undefined on the sync path and reading `.error` throws, breaking the Zoho CRM token refresh flow. The same inconsistency (axios Response vs fetch Response shapes) applies to zoho-bigin too.

judged_text: zohoCrmTokenInfo comes from axios ({data}) in the fallback path but is a fetch Response in sync mode, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined in sync mode. With credential sync enabled, the !zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error guard throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined' on the sync path, crashing the Zoho CRM refresh flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it returns the result of `fetch(...)` (a `Response`). In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is assigned from `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` but later treated as an Axios response via `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. On the sync path `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` will be `undefined` (since `Response` has no `.data`), so the guard `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` will throw at runtime.
